title: Analyzing Palmer Penguins Using R
text:
In this post, I use R to explore the Palmer Penguins dataset. I look at body mass across penguin species and examine the relationship between flipper length and body mass.
The data comes from the Palmer Penguins project, which uses data from the Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

title: Analyzing Palmer Penguins Using R
text:
Body mass by species
I calculated the average body mass for each penguin species to compare their typical body sizes.

avg_species_mass <- aggregate(body_mass_g ~ species, data = penguins, FUN = mean, na.rm = TRUE)

avg_species_mass

    species body_mass_g
1    Adelie    3700.662
2 Chinstrap    3733.088
3    Gentoo    5076.016

title: Analyzing Palmer Penguins Using R
text:
Summary statistics

summary_by_species <- aggregate(
  cbind(flipper_length_mm, body_mass_g) ~ species,
  data = penguins,
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

summary_by_species

    species flipper_length_mm body_mass_g
1    Adelie          189.9536    3700.662
2 Chinstrap          195.8235    3733.088
3    Gentoo          217.1870    5076.016

title: Analyzing Palmer Penguins Using R
text:
Flipper length and body mass
This figure shows the relationship between flipper length and body mass for the three penguin species.

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(penguins, aes(x = flipper_length_mm, y = body_mass_g, color = species, shape = species)) +
geom_point() +
scale_color_manual(values = c(
"Adelie" = "#A8DADC",
"Chinstrap" = "#F4A6A6",
"Gentoo" = "#CDB4DB"
)) +
labs(
x = "Flipper length (mm)",
y = "Body mass (g)",
color = "Species",
shape = "Species"
)

Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
(`geom_point()`).








Figure 1: Flipper length and body mass of Palmer Penguins, by species.

title: Analyzing Palmer Penguins Using R
text:
Findings
Based on the graph, it is clear that flipper length tends to increase as body mass increases. In particular, Gentoo are the largest penguin species and have both the heaviest body mass and the longest flipper length.

title: Analyzing Palmer Penguins Data Using Python
text:
Flipper length and body mass
The following graph demonstrates the relationship between flipper lengths and body mass. The different colours and shapes depict the different species.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
adelie = penguins[penguins["species"] == "Adelie"]
chinstrap = penguins[penguins["species"] == "Chinstrap"]
gentoo = penguins[penguins["species"] == "Gentoo"]

plt.scatter(adelie["flipper_length_mm"], adelie["body_mass_g"],
color="#A8DADC", marker="o", label="Adelie")

plt.scatter(chinstrap["flipper_length_mm"], chinstrap["body_mass_g"],
color="#F4A6A6", marker="s", label="Chinstrap")

plt.scatter(gentoo["flipper_length_mm"], gentoo["body_mass_g"],
color="#CDB4DB", marker="^", label="Gentoo")

plt.xlabel("Flipper length (mm)")
plt.ylabel("Body mass (g)")
plt.legend()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Flipper length and body mass of Palmer Penguins, by species.

title: Analyzing Palmer Penguins Data Using Python
text:
Findings
Based on the graph, it is clear that flipper length tends to increase as body mass increases. In particular, Gentoo are the largest penguin species and have both the heaviest body mass and the longest flipper length.
